category: POSTFEKO Lua API (extended): application, results, data sets, graphs, views and exports
description: Object-level reference for the POSTFEKO Lua API (pf namespace) beyond the overview in 05: the application and model objects, every result collection of a solution configuration and the data sets they return, the DataSet/Complex/Matrix helpers, math scripts and stored data, 2D graphs, traces, annotations, 3D views, animations and all export paths. Names come from the installed 2026.1 API reference and were run headless with 'postfeko --non-interactive --run-script' against a solved dipole and the example models shipped in FEKO_HOME/shared/Resources/Automation; notes say what was run-verified.

tools.name: pf namespace and result-type namespaces (pf.GetApplication, pf.FarField, pf.Excitation, pf.NearField, pf.SParameter ...)
tools.description: pf is the POSTFEKO scripting namespace. Apart from pf.GetApplication() it mainly holds object classes (pf.DataSet, pf.Complex, pf.Matrix, pf.ComplexMatrix, pf.Point, pf.Interpolator, pf.Launcher, pf.Form, pf.Enums) and one static namespace per result type: pf.FarField, pf.NearField, pf.Excitation, pf.SParameter, pf.Power, pf.Load, pf.Network, pf.SAR, pf.CharacteristicModes, pf.SurfaceCurrentsAndCharges, pf.WireCurrentsAndCharges, pf.TRCoefficients, pf.ReciprocalExcitation, pf.CustomData, plus the utility namespaces pf.MatIO, pf.Archive and pf.DRE. The result namespaces fetch data by a 'model.configuration.request' path string, which is what math scripts use.
tools.usage:
app = pf.GetApplication()
names = pf.<ResultType>.GetNames()             -- list of 'model.config.request' strings
ds = pf.<ResultType>.GetDataSet(name)
ds = pf.<ResultType>.GetDataSet(name, samples)  -- continuous frequency axis only
ds = pf.<ResultType>.GetDataSet(name, startFreq, endFreq, samples)
ds = pf.NearField.GetMediaDataSet(name)
ds = pf.FarField.GetSampledDataSet(name, thetaStart, thetaEnd, thetaCount, phiStart, phiEnd, phiCount)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Result path 'model.configuration.request', e.g. 'dipole300.StandardConfiguration1.VoltageSource1'; copy it from GetNames().

parameters.name: samples
parameters.description: Number of frequency samples; only allowed when the frequency axis is continuous (adaptive frequency sampling), otherwise Error 17421.

parameters.name: startFreq, endFreq
parameters.description: Frequency sub-range in Hz for continuous results.

tools.example:
for _, n in ipairs(pf.FarField.GetNames()) do print(n) end
-- dipole300.StandardConfiguration1.FarField1
ds = pf.FarField.GetDataSet("dipole300.StandardConfiguration1.FarField1")
z = pf.Excitation.GetDataSet("dipole300.StandardConfiguration1.VoltageSource1")[1].Impedance
print(z.re, z.im)
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: GetNames for FarField/Excitation/Power/NearField/SParameter/SAR/CharacteristicModes/SurfaceCurrentsAndCharges/WireCurrentsAndCharges/Network/Load, GetDataSet(path), and 'The frequency axis must be continuous to be sampled' for GetDataSet(path, 11) on a single-frequency model. The power result path ends in '.Power'. pf.Source does not exist (use pf.Excitation); namespace names are plural where shown (CharacteristicModes, TRCoefficients, SurfaceCurrentsAndCharges).

tools.name: POSTFEKO Application object (Version, SessionPath, OpenFile, NewProject, SaveAs .pfs, window management)
tools.description: The object returned by pf.GetApplication() owns the session: the Models, graph, view, math-script, stored-data, imported-data and report collections, plus session and window methods. OpenFile loads a .fek/.bof pair (or a .pfs session), NewProject clears the session, SaveAs writes a .pfs session and CascadeWindows/TileWindows/CloseAllWindows arrange windows. Read-only properties report the version, session name/path, modified state and whether Microsoft Word/PowerPoint are installed for reports.
tools.usage:
app = pf.GetApplication()
app:OpenFile(filename) | app:NewProject() | app:Save() | app:SaveAs("session.pfs") | app:ReloadChangedFiles()
app:CascadeWindows() | app:TileWindows() | app:CloseAllWindows() | app:Undo() | app:Redo() | app:Close()
app.Version.Major/Minor/Patch/Build, app.SessionName, app.SessionPath, app.Modified, app.MSWordInstalled, app.MSPowerPointInstalled
Collections: Models, CartesianGraphs, PolarGraphs, SmithCharts, CartesianSurfaceGraphs, Views, Windows, MathScripts, StoredData, ImportedDataSets, Reports

parameters.name: OpenFile(filename)
parameters.description: Opens a model (.fek with its .bof) or session file; opening a model that is already in the session fails with Error 16302.

parameters.name: SaveAs(filename)
parameters.description: Saves the session (.pfs): graphs, views, math scripts, stored and imported data.

parameters.name: ReloadChangedFiles()
parameters.description: Reloads models/imports whose files changed; not done automatically while a script runs.

tools.example:
app = pf.GetApplication()
local v = app.Version
print(v.Major .. "." .. v.Minor .. "." .. v.Patch .. " build " .. v.Build)  -- 2026.1.0 build 8642
local ok, err = pcall(function() app:OpenFile([[D:/work/dipole300.fek]]) end)
if not ok then print(err) end  -- Error 16302 if already loaded
app:SaveAs([[D:/work/results.pfs]])
print(app.SessionName)  -- results
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: Version, SessionPath (the working directory until a session is saved), MSWordInstalled, OpenFile, Error 16302 when the file given on the postfeko command line is opened again, SaveAs .pfs (SessionName then returns the base name, Modified false), TileWindows, CloseAllWindows (Windows.Count becomes 0) and NewProject (Models.Count 0). When the .fek is passed on the command line it is already loaded before the script starts, so scripts should not OpenFile it again.

tools.name: Model object (Label, GetPath, Configurations, Launcher, ReassociateModel, Delete)
tools.description: A Model is one loaded solved model (.fek + .bof), found in app.Models by index or label (the file base name). It exposes the configuration collection, the directory of its files, and a Launcher that can re-run the Feko components for that model from POSTFEKO. ReassociateModel points the model at a different set of files (for example after re-solving a copy) and Delete removes it together with its plots and traces.
tools.usage:
m = app.Models[1] | app.Models["dipole300"]
m.Label; m:GetPath(); m.Configurations[i]; m.Launcher:RunFEKO(); m.Launcher:GetCommandRunFEKO(); m:ReassociateModel(filename); m:Delete()

parameters.name: Configurations
parameters.description: ConfigurationCollection of SolutionConfiguration objects (index or label such as 'StandardConfiguration1').

parameters.name: Launcher
parameters.description: Launcher object with RunFEKO/RunPREFEKO/RunOPTFEKO (return LaunchResult), RunCADFEKO/RunEDITFEKO/RunPOSTFEKO (return boolean), GetCommandRun* strings and Settings (ComponentLaunchOptions).

tools.example:
m = app.Models["dipole300"]
print(m.Label, m:GetPath())
print(m.Launcher:GetCommandRunFEKO())
-- C:/Program Files/Altair/2026.1/feko/bin/runfeko dipole300 --run-from-gui -np all --parallel-authenticate localonly
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: Label, GetPath (returns the folder, not the file), Launcher.Type, Launcher.Settings.Type = ComponentLaunchOptions, GetCommandRunFEKO output above, and indexing app.Models by label. ReassociateModel and Delete are from the API reference (ReassociateModel exists as a function in 2026.1 but was not called).

tools.name: SolutionConfiguration object (StartFrequency, EndFrequency, Mesh, result collections, ExportFarFields/ExportNearFields)
tools.description: Each configuration of a model holds the results solved for it. Properties give the frequency span, whether it is a frequency configuration, its label and the Mesh; collections hold one ResultData object per request. ExportFarFields and ExportNearFields write every far field (.ffe) or near field (.efe/.hfe) of the configuration in one call.
tools.usage:
cfg = m.Configurations[1] | m.Configurations["SParameterConfiguration1"]
cfg.StartFrequency; cfg.EndFrequency; cfg.FrequencyConfiguration; cfg.Label; cfg.Mesh; cfg.Model
Collections: Excitations, Loads, FarFields, NearFields, SParameters, Power, FarFieldPowerIntegrals, NearFieldPowerIntegrals, SurfaceCurrents, WireCurrents, CharacteristicModes, ReceivingAntennas, ReciprocalExcitations, SAR, ErrorEstimates, SpiceProbes, Networks, TransmissionLines, TRCoefficients, Rays
cfg:ExportFarFields(filename, pf.Enums.FarFieldsExportTypeEnum.X, samples)
cfg:ExportNearFields(filename, pf.Enums.NearFieldsExportTypeEnum.X, samples)

parameters.name: Power / CharacteristicModes / Rays
parameters.description: Singular-result collections holding at most one item (cfg.Power[1]).

parameters.name: samples
parameters.description: Export sample count, at least 2 (1 is rejected).

tools.example:
cfg = app.Models[1].Configurations[1]
print(cfg.Label, cfg.StartFrequency, cfg.EndFrequency)  -- StandardConfiguration1 3e8 3e8
for _, c in ipairs({"Excitations", "FarFields", "NearFields", "Power", "SurfaceCurrents"}) do
  print(c, cfg[c].Count)
end
cfg:ExportFarFields([[D:/work/all_ff]], pf.Enums.FarFieldsExportTypeEnum.Directivity, 2)
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: all 20 collections listed exist; cfg.Sources, cfg.Currents and cfg.Powers are nil. ExportFarFields with 2 samples wrote all_ff.ffe; ExportNearFields with NearFieldsExportTypeEnum.Both fails with 'Error 17196: No magnetic near field data to export' when only E was requested. A characteristic-mode configuration is labelled 'CharacteristicModeConfiguration1'.

tools.name: Collection objects (Count, Item, Items, Contains, UniqueName, label indexing)
tools.description: Every POSTFEKO collection (ModelCollection, ConfigurationCollection, FarFieldCollection, ResultTraceCollection, ViewCollection, MathScriptCollection ...) supports the same access pattern: Count, numeric or label indexing, Item(), Items() returning a Lua list, Contains(label) and UniqueName(label). Collections that create objects add an Add method (CartesianGraphs:Add(), Traces:Add(result), Plots:Add(result), Views:Add([configuration]), MathScripts:Add(type), Reports:Add(template, type)).
tools.usage: coll.Count; coll[i]; coll["Label"]; coll:Item(i); coll:Item("Label"); coll:Items(); coll:Contains("Label"); coll:UniqueName("Label")

parameters.name: Items()
parameters.description: Returns a Lua list of the objects, usable with ipairs or printlist.

parameters.name: Contains(label)
parameters.description: True when an item with this label exists; safer than indexing a missing label.

tools.example:
for _, ff in ipairs(cfg.FarFields:Items()) do print(ff.Label, ff.Type) end
if app.CartesianGraphs:Contains("GainCut") then g = app.CartesianGraphs["GainCut"] end
print(app.Models["startup"].Configurations[1].Label)
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: Count on all result collections, label indexing on Models, Configurations and CartesianGraphs (a graph is indexed by its WindowTitle). Result labels are the request names from CADFEKO (FarField1, VoltageSource1, Currents1); some results get generated labels such as 'Currents1_1' for the wire part of a currents request.

tools.name: FarFieldData object (GetDataSet, GetSampledDataSet, ExportData, StoreData, continuous axes)
tools.description: A far-field request result in cfg.FarFields. GetDataSet returns axes Frequency, Theta, Phi (plus Mode for characteristic-mode configurations) with the complex far-field components and the scalar gain/directivity factors. For continuous results (adaptive frequency or continuous theta/phi), GetSampledDataSet re-samples the pattern on any theta/phi grid; ExportData writes a .ffe file and StoreData makes a session copy.
tools.usage:
ff = cfg.FarFields[1]
ds = ff:GetDataSet() | ff:GetDataSet(samples) | ff:GetDataSet(fStart, fEnd, samples)
ds = ff:GetSampledDataSet(thetaStart, thetaEnd, thetaCount, phiStart, phiEnd, phiCount)
ff:ExportData(filename, pf.Enums.FarFieldsExportTypeEnum.Gain, samples)
ff:StoreData(); ff.ContinuousFrequencyAxis; ff.ContinuousThetaAxis; ff.ContinuousPhiAxis; ff.DataSetAvailable

parameters.name: FarFieldsExportTypeEnum
parameters.description: Gain, Directivity, RCS, RealisedGain ... selects the quantity written to the .ffe.

parameters.name: samples
parameters.description: At least 2; for discrete results the solved points are written regardless.

parameters.name: GetSampledDataSet counts
parameters.description: Number of theta and phi samples between the given start/end angles (degrees).

tools.example:
ff = cfg.FarFields[1]
ff:ExportData([[D:/work/dipole_ff]], pf.Enums.FarFieldsExportTypeEnum.Gain, 2)  -- writes dipole_ff.ffe
for i = 1, cfg.FarFields.Count do
  local f = cfg.FarFields[i]
  if f.ContinuousThetaAxis then
    local d = f:GetSampledDataSet(0, 180, 91, 0, 0, 1)
    print(f.Label, d.Axes["Theta"].Count)  -- 91
  end
end
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: GetDataSet axes/quantities, ExportData with 2 samples (1 raises '1 is an invalid sample count. The least number of samples allowed is 2.'), a string-only ExportData call is rejected, StoreData returns FarFieldStoredData, and GetSampledDataSet on the continuous far field of the shipped helix_6_2_PBC_1x1_ContinuousFarField example.

tools.name: Far-field data set quantities and the gain formula (EFieldTheta, EFieldPhi, GainFactor, DirectivityFactor, RealisedGainFactor)
tools.description: A far-field data set stores the complex components EFieldTheta and EFieldPhi (unit V) and three scalar factors, not gain values. Gain, directivity and realised gain are obtained by multiplying |Etheta|^2 + |Ephi|^2 by GainFactor, DirectivityFactor or RealisedGainFactor respectively; convert with 10*log10 for dBi. Imported .ffe data sets carry EFieldTheta, EFieldPhi, DirectivityFactor and GainFactor.
tools.usage:
p = ds[iFreq][iTheta][iPhi]
G = (p.EFieldTheta:Magnitude()^2 + p.EFieldPhi:Magnitude()^2) * p.GainFactor
G_dBi = 10*math.log10(G)

parameters.name: EFieldTheta, EFieldPhi
parameters.description: Complex far-field components (Complex, V; r*E normalised).

parameters.name: DirectivityFactor
parameters.description: Scale factor giving directivity (uses radiated power).

parameters.name: GainFactor
parameters.description: Scale factor giving gain (uses input power, so losses count).

parameters.name: RealisedGainFactor
parameters.description: Scale factor giving realised gain (also includes source mismatch).

tools.example:
ds = cfg.FarFields[1]:GetDataSet()
local p = ds[1][19][1]  -- theta = 90 deg, phi = 0
local e2 = p.EFieldTheta:Magnitude()^2 + p.EFieldPhi:Magnitude()^2
print(string.format("%.2f dBi", 10*math.log10(e2 * p.GainFactor)))  -- 2.12 dBi for a half-wave dipole
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: for the dipole at theta=90 deg GainFactor = 2.309 alone would suggest 3.63 dBi, but the formula gives 2.12 dBi, identical to the gain trace in a Cartesian graph and to the help page 'DataSet Structure: Gain'. Do not treat GainFactor itself as the gain.

tools.name: Source result objects (SourceVoltageSegment, SourceVoltageEdge, SourceVoltageVertex, SourceWaveguide, SourcePlaneWave ...)
tools.description: cfg.Excitations holds ExcitationData specialisations named after the source type: SourceVoltageSegment (wire port), SourceVoltageEdge, SourceVoltageVertex, SourceVoltageCable, SourceVoltageNetwork, SourceCoaxial, SourceMagneticFrill, SourceWaveguide, SourceModal, SourcePlaneWave, SourceElectricDipole, SourceMagneticDipole, SourceRadiationPattern, SourceSphericalModes, SourceAperture, SourcePCB and others. Port-type sources return a data set with Impedance, Admittance, Voltage, Current (complex), Power (W), MismatchLoss and SourceType per frequency and can export Touchstone data; field sources such as plane waves have no GetDataSet.
tools.usage:
ex = cfg.Excitations[1]; ex.Type; ex.Label; ex.ReferenceImpedance
ds = ex:GetDataSet() | ex:GetDataSet(samples) | ex:GetDataSet(fStart, fEnd, samples)
ex:ExportData(filename, pf.Enums.FrequencyUnitEnum.MHz, pf.Enums.NetworkParameterTypeEnum.Scattering, pf.Enums.NetworkParameterFormatEnum.RI, referenceImpedance, samples)

parameters.name: ReferenceImpedance
parameters.description: Port reference impedance as an expression (prints '50 + j*0').

parameters.name: Impedance / Admittance / Voltage / Current
parameters.description: Complex per-frequency quantities (Ohm, S, V, A).

parameters.name: Power
parameters.description: Source power in W (scalar).

parameters.name: MismatchLoss, SourceType
parameters.description: Scalar mismatch loss and an enum value identifying the source kind.

tools.example:
ex = cfg.Excitations[1]
print(ex.Type, ex.Label, ex.ReferenceImpedance)  -- SourceVoltageSegment VoltageSource1 50 + j*0
ds = ex:GetDataSet()
for i = 1, ds.Axes["Frequency"].Count do
  local z = ds[i].Impedance
  print(ds.Axes["Frequency"]:ValueAt(i), z.re, z.im)
end
ex:ExportData([[D:/work/dipole_s]], pf.Enums.FrequencyUnitEnum.MHz, pf.Enums.NetworkParameterTypeEnum.Scattering, pf.Enums.NetworkParameterFormatEnum.RI, 50, 2)  -- dipole_s.s1p
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: Types SourceVoltageSegment, SourceVoltageEdge, SourceVoltageVertex, SourceVoltageCable, SourceWaveguide and SourcePlaneWave seen in shipped examples; quantities as listed with units; SourcePlaneWave has no GetDataSet method; ExportData wrote a .s1p. GetDataSet(11) on a discrete frequency axis fails with Error 17421.

tools.name: NearFieldData object (GetDataSet, GetMediaDataSet, ExportData .efe/.hfe)
tools.description: A near-field request result in cfg.NearFields. Its data set has axes Frequency and the three spatial axes of the request (X/Y/Z in m for Cartesian requests) and quantities EFieldComp1..3 (complex V/m, or HFieldComp1..3 for H requests) plus MediumIndex. GetMediaDataSet returns the medium properties at each point (RelativePermittivity, RelativePermeability, LossTangent, MagneticLossTangent, MassDensity, Conductivity) with the medium names in MetaData.MediumNames; ExportData writes .efe/.hfe files.
tools.usage:
nf = cfg.NearFields[1]
ds = nf:GetDataSet() | nf:GetDataSet(samples) | nf:GetDataSet(fStart, fEnd, samples)
mds = nf:GetMediaDataSet()
nf:ExportData(filename, pf.Enums.NearFieldsExportTypeEnum.Electric | Magnetic | Both, samples)

parameters.name: EFieldComp1/2/3
parameters.description: Complex field components in the request coordinate system (Cartesian: x, y, z).

parameters.name: MediumIndex
parameters.description: Index into MetaData.MediumNames of the media data set.

parameters.name: samples
parameters.description: Only meaningful for continuous frequency results; e.g. GetDataSet(101) re-samples 101 frequencies.

tools.example:
nf = cfg.NearFields[1]
ds = nf:GetDataSet(7e9, 8e9, 11)
local e = ds[1][13][10][1].EFieldComp3
print(e:Magnitude(), e:Phase())
nf:ExportData([[D:/work/startup_nf]], pf.Enums.NearFieldsExportTypeEnum.Electric, 51)  -- startup_nf.efe
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1 with the shipped startup.fek (continuous frequency): axes Frequency/X/Y/Z, quantities EFieldComp1..3 + MediumIndex, GetDataSet(101) and GetDataSet(7e9, 8e9, 11), GetMediaDataSet quantity names, ExportData .efe. Exporting Both when no H field was solved raises Error 17196.

tools.name: SurfaceCurrentsData and WireCurrentsData (GetDataSet, ExportData .os/.ol)
tools.description: A currents request produces a SurfaceCurrentsData item (triangles) and/or a WireCurrentsData item (segments). Surface-current data sets have axes Frequency and MeshIndex with ElectricX/Y/Z (A/m) and Charge (C/m^2); wire-current data sets have Frequency and MeshIndex with Current (A) and Charge (C/m). For characteristic-mode configurations a Mode axis is inserted. ExportData writes the currents/charges as .os (surface) and .ol (wire) text files.
tools.usage:
sc = cfg.SurfaceCurrents[1]; wc = cfg.WireCurrents[1]
ds = sc:GetDataSet(); ds[iFreq][iTriangle].ElectricX
sc:ExportData(filename, pf.Enums.CurrentsExportTypeEnum.Both, samples)
plot = app.Views[1].Plots:Add(sc)  -- SurfaceCurrents3DPlot

parameters.name: MeshIndex
parameters.description: Triangle or segment index in the configuration mesh (see cfg.Mesh).

parameters.name: CurrentsExportTypeEnum
parameters.description: Which values to export (Both = currents and charges).

tools.example:
sc = cfg.SurfaceCurrents["Currents1"]
ds = sc:GetDataSet()
local jx = ds[1][1].ElectricX
print(ds.Axes["MeshIndex"].Count, jx:Magnitude())
sc:ExportData([[D:/work/startup_currents]], pf.Enums.CurrentsExportTypeEnum.Both, 11)  -- writes .os and .ol
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1 (startup.fek: 222 mesh indices, 11 frequencies; CharacteristicModes.fek: axes Frequency, Mode, MeshIndex). The export produced both startup_currents.os and startup_currents.ol. A currents request covering wires and faces appears as two items, e.g. 'Currents1' and 'Currents1_1'.

tools.name: SParameterData object (S-parameter axis, SParameter/Load/PortFlag quantities, Touchstone ExportData)
tools.description: S-parameter results live in the S-parameter configuration (cfg.SParameters). The data set has axes Frequency and 'S-parameter' whose values are strings like 'S1,1', 'S2,1', with quantities SParameter (complex), Load (reference impedance, Ohm) and PortFlag. ExportData writes a Touchstone file whose extension (.s2p, .s3p ...) follows the port count, in the chosen frequency unit, parameter type and format.
tools.usage:
sp = cfg.SParameters[1]
ds = sp:GetDataSet(); ds.Axes["S-parameter"]:ValueAt(i); ds[iFreq][iPair].SParameter
sp:ExportData(filename, pf.Enums.FrequencyUnitEnum.GHz, pf.Enums.NetworkParameterTypeEnum.Scattering, pf.Enums.NetworkParameterFormatEnum.DB | MA | RI, referenceImpedance, samples)

parameters.name: S-parameter axis
parameters.description: String values 'Si,j' for the excited port j and receiving port i.

parameters.name: NetworkParameterFormatEnum
parameters.description: DB, MA or RI (the only three members in 2026.1).

parameters.name: referenceImpedance
parameters.description: Optional renormalisation impedance; omit the argument to keep the solved reference.

tools.example:
sp = app.Models["Waveguide_Divider"].Configurations["SParameterConfiguration1"].SParameters[1]
ds = sp:GetDataSet()
for i = 1, ds.Axes["S-parameter"].Count do
  print(ds.Axes["S-parameter"]:ValueAt(i), ds[1][i].SParameter:Magnitude())
end  -- S1,1 0.023  S2,1 0.707  S3,1 0.707
sp:ExportData([[D:/work/divider]], pf.Enums.FrequencyUnitEnum.GHz, pf.Enums.NetworkParameterTypeEnum.Scattering, pf.Enums.NetworkParameterFormatEnum.DB, 50, 2)
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1 with the shipped Waveguide_Divider.fek: axes, quantity names, values and a written divider.s3p. On graphs the S-parameter is chosen with trace:SetFixedAxisValue("S-parameter", "S2,1"); SParameterQuantity has no Type property.

tools.name: PowerData, FarFieldPowerIntegralData and NearFieldPowerIntegralData
tools.description: cfg.Power[1] (label 'Power') gives ActivePower, PowerLoss (W) and Efficiency per frequency, and its data set metadata carries the power-scaling settings (PowerScaling, SourcePower, Impedance). cfg.FarFieldPowerIntegrals holds one item per far-field request with TotalRadiatedPower (W) integrated over the requested sphere or cut. cfg.NearFieldPowerIntegrals items exist for near-field requests but have no GetDataSet in 2026.1, so plot them on graphs instead.
tools.usage:
pd = cfg.Power[1]:GetDataSet(); pd[i].ActivePower; pd[i].PowerLoss; pd[i].Efficiency; pd.MetaData.PowerScaling
fp = cfg.FarFieldPowerIntegrals[1]:GetDataSet(); fp[i].TotalRadiatedPower
pf.Power.GetDataSet("model.StandardConfiguration1.Power")

parameters.name: ActivePower
parameters.description: Active input power (W).

parameters.name: PowerLoss
parameters.description: Losses in media, loads and finite conductivity (W).

parameters.name: Efficiency
parameters.description: Ratio used for gain versus directivity (1 for lossless).

parameters.name: TotalRadiatedPower
parameters.description: Far-field power integral (W).

tools.example:
pd = cfg.Power[1]:GetDataSet()
print(pd[1].ActivePower, pd[1].PowerLoss, pd[1].Efficiency)  -- 0.00722 0 1 for a lossless dipole fed with 1 V
fp = cfg.FarFieldPowerIntegrals["FarField1"]:GetDataSet()
print(fp[1].TotalRadiatedPower)
print(tostring(pd.MetaData.PowerScaling))  -- NoPowerScaling
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: quantity names and units, metadata PowerScaling = NoPowerScaling and SourcePower = 0 for an unscaled model, FarFieldPowerIntegral quantity TotalRadiatedPower, NearFieldPowerIntegralData without GetDataSet. A Power trace defaults to quantity ActivePower (PowerQuantityTypeEnum: ActivePower, Efficiency, LossPower).

tools.name: CharacteristicModeData object (EigenValue, ModalExcitationCoefficient, Mode axis, 'Mode index' trace axis)
tools.description: Characteristic-mode configurations expose cfg.CharacteristicModes[1] whose data set has axes Frequency and Mode with the complex EigenValue and ModalExcitationCoefficient. Far fields, currents, loads, networks and transmission lines of the same configuration gain a Mode axis, so modal patterns and currents are indexed per mode. On graphs the mode is selected through the trace axis named 'Mode index' (or 'Mode index (untracked)').
tools.usage:
cm = cfg.CharacteristicModes[1]; ds = cm:GetDataSet(); ds[iFreq][iMode].EigenValue
t = g.Traces:Add(cm); t.Quantity.Type = pf.Enums.CharacteristicModeQuantityTypeEnum.ModalSignificance; t.IndependentAxis = "Mode index" | "Frequency"

parameters.name: EigenValue
parameters.description: Complex eigenvalue lambda_n (real part used for modal significance 1/|1+j*lambda|).

parameters.name: ModalExcitationCoefficient
parameters.description: Complex coefficient when an excitation is present.

parameters.name: Mode index
parameters.description: Trace axis name for the mode; the data-set axis itself is called 'Mode'.

tools.example:
cm = app.Models["CharacteristicModes"].Configurations[1].CharacteristicModes[1]
ds = cm:GetDataSet()
for m = 1, ds.Axes["Mode"].Count do print(m, ds[1][m].EigenValue.re) end
t = app.CartesianGraphs:Add().Traces:Add(cm)
t.Quantity.Type = pf.Enums.CharacteristicModeQuantityTypeEnum.ModalSignificance
print(t.IndependentAxis)  -- Mode index
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1 with the shipped CharacteristicModes.fek: axes Frequency/Mode, quantities, far-field axes Frequency/Mode/Theta/Phi, surface-current axes Frequency/Mode/MeshIndex, trace IndependentAxesAvailable 'Frequency, Mode index, Mode index (untracked)'. SetFixedAxisValue("Mode", ...) fails ('Unable to retrieve the Mode axis') - use the trace axis name 'Mode index'.

tools.name: SARData object (HasPeakSAR, PeakSARInCube, AverageSAROverTotalVolume, MassOfPeakSARCube)
tools.description: Each SAR request gives one SARData item whose data set (axis Frequency) reports flags telling which values were computed and the values themselves: HasPeakSAR, HasAverageSAROverTotalVolume, HasAverageSAROverRequestedVolume (booleans), MassOfPeakSARCube (kg), AirFractionOfPeakSARCube, PeakSARInCube, AverageSAROverTotalVolume and AverageSAROverRequestedVolume (W/kg). Only requests that computed a peak SAR cube can be shown in a 3D view.
tools.usage:
sar = cfg.SAR[1]; d = sar:GetDataSet(); if d[1].HasPeakSAR then print(d[1].PeakSARInCube) end
pf.SAR.GetDataSet("SAR_Example.StandardConfiguration1.SAR1")

tools.name: DataSet indexing rules and DataSetIndexer (ds[i][j][k], ds[{i,j,k}], AxisValue, AxisIndex, Error 17435)

Each partial index returns a DataSetIndexer whose AxisValue(name|index), AxisIndex, AxisName and AxisUnit methods tell where the point lies. Reading or writing a quantity before all axes are indexed raises Error 17435.

v = ds[iFreq][iTheta][iPhi].GainFactor
v = ds[{iFreq, iTheta, iPhi}].GainFactor
idx = ds[1][19][1]; idx:AxisValue("Theta"); idx:AxisIndex("Theta"); idx:AxisName(2); idx:AxisUnit("Theta")
ds[1][19][1].EFieldTheta = pf.Complex(1, 0)  -- write

parameters.name: index order
parameters.description: Same as ds.Axes order (Frequency first for solver results).

parameters.name: AxisValue(name)
parameters.description: Axis value at the current point, in the axis unit (deg for angles, m for positions, Hz for frequency).

tools.example:
local p = ds[1][19][1]
print(p:AxisValue("Theta"), p:AxisIndex("Theta"))  -- 90 19
print(ds[{1, 19, 1}].GainFactor)
local ok, err = pcall(function() return ds[1][19].GainFactor end)
print(err)  -- Error 17435: Quantities can only be set once all of the axes have been indexed.

tools.name: Building data sets (pf.DataSet.New, Axes:Add, Quantities:Add, pf.DataSet.ForAllValues, pf.DataSet.CombineDataSets)
tools.description: Custom data sets are created with pf.DataSet.New(), then given axes (standard DataSetAxisEnum axes or free-named axes with a unit) and quantities, and filled by indexing or with the iterator pf.DataSet.ForAllValues(fn, ds), which calls fn(index, ds) for every point. pf.DataSet.CombineDataSets(name, unit, values, sets) stacks data sets of identical structure along a new outer axis, e.g. to combine parameter-sweep runs. Store the result with StoreData(pf.Enums.StoredDataTypeEnum.Custom) to plot it.
tools.usage:
d = pf.DataSet.New()
d.Axes:Add(pf.Enums.DataSetAxisEnum.Frequency, "Hz", start, stop, count)
d.Axes:Add("Index", "", 1, 3, 3)                      -- free-named axis
d.Quantities:Add("Y", pf.Enums.DataSetQuantityTypeEnum.Scalar | Complex, unit)
pf.DataSet.ForAllValues(function(index, ds) ds[index].Y = 1 end, d)
c = pf.DataSet.CombineDataSets("Case", "", {1, 2}, {d1, d2})

parameters.name: Axes:Add overloads
parameters.description: (enum), (enum, start, stop, count), (enum, list), (name, unit), (name, unit, value), (name, unit, start, stop, count), (name, unit, list), (axis).

parameters.name: ForAllValues(fn, ds, ...)
parameters.description: fn receives an opaque index usable as ds[index]; extra arguments are passed through.

tools.example:
d = pf.DataSet.New()
d.Axes:Add(pf.Enums.DataSetAxisEnum.Frequency, "Hz", 1e8, 3e8, 3)
d.Quantities:Add("Y", pf.Enums.DataSetQuantityTypeEnum.Scalar, "")
for i = 1, #d.Axes["Frequency"] do d[i].Y = i end
s = d:StoreData(pf.Enums.StoredDataTypeEnum.Custom)
t = app.CartesianGraphs:Add().Traces:Add(s)  -- CustomDataTrace
c = pf.DataSet.CombineDataSets("Case", "", {1, 2}, {cfg.Excitations[1]:GetDataSet(), cfg.Excitations[1]:GetDataSet()})
-- c axes: Case, Frequency

tools.name: pf.Complex (complex numbers, i and j constants, Magnitude, Phase, static maths)
tools.description: Complex values returned by data sets and used in math scripts are pf.Complex objects with read/write .re and .im fields, methods Magnitude/Abs, Phase/Angle (radians), Real, Imag, Conj/Conjugate, IsInfinite, IsNotANumber, and arithmetic operators. The global constants i and j equal sqrt(-1), so 2 + j*1 builds a complex number. Static functions (pf.Complex.Sqrt, Exponent, Log, Log10, Power, Sin, Cos, Tan, Asin, Acos, Atan, Floor, Ceil, IsEqual) work on complex arguments.
tools.usage:
c = pf.Complex(re, im) | pf.Complex.New(re, im) | re + j*im
c.re; c.im; c:Magnitude(); c:Phase(); c:Conj(); pf.Complex.Sqrt(c); pf.Complex.Power(c, n)

parameters.name: Phase()
parameters.description: Phase in radians; multiply by 180/math.pi for degrees.

parameters.name: c[1], c[2]
parameters.description: Index access to the real and imaginary parts.

z = cfg.Excitations[1]:GetDataSet()[1].Impedance
local gamma = (z - 50) / (z + 50)
print(20*math.log10(gamma:Magnitude()), "dB")
print(pf.Complex.Sqrt(pf.Complex(-4, 0)))  -- 0 + 2i
print(i)  -- 0 + 1i

tools.name: pf.Matrix, pf.ComplexMatrix and pf.Interpolator
tools.description: pf.Matrix and pf.ComplexMatrix are fast dense matrices for vectorised post-processing: constructors New(rows, cols[, fill]), Identity, Zeros, Ones, Diagonal; methods Transpose, Inverse, Determinant, SubMatrix, ReplaceSubMatrix, FFT/IFFT, Abs, Phase, Max/Min/Mean/Sum, ExportMatFile; element-wise static functions (MultiplyByElement, GreaterThan, Find, Log10 ...). pf.Interpolator.Rational(x, y) fits a rational function to scalar or complex samples and Resample(newX) evaluates it, which is useful to densify sparse frequency data.
tools.usage:
m = pf.Matrix.New(rows, cols, fill); m[r][c]; m.RowCount; m:Inverse(); m:FFT()
cm = pf.ComplexMatrix.Identity(n)
it = pf.Interpolator.Rational(xList, yList); vals = it:Resample(newXList); it.Succeeded

parameters.name: Resample(list)
parameters.description: Returns a Lua list of interpolated values at the requested independent values.

parameters.name: Succeeded / Errors / Warnings
parameters.description: Interpolator fit status strings.

tools.example:
m = pf.Matrix.New(2, 2, 1)
print(m.RowCount, m:Sum())  -- 2 4
print(pf.Matrix.Identity(3):Determinant())  -- 1
it = pf.Interpolator.Rational({1, 2, 3, 4}, {1, 4, 9, 16})
print(it.Succeeded, it:Resample({2.5})[1])  -- true 6.25
g = cfg.FarFields[1]:GetDataSet():ToMatrix({"GainFactor"})
print(g:Max())
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: Matrix.New/Sum/RowCount, Identity/Determinant, ComplexMatrix.Identity, Interpolator.Rational + Resample, ToMatrix + Max. A trace's Values property is also a Matrix (column 1 independent axis, column 2 values).

mesh:GetPointMatrixForTriangleMeshIndexList({1, 2})

tools.name: MathScript objects (app.MathScripts:Add, Script, Run, GetDataSet, StoreData, FarFieldMathScript, CustomMathScript)
tools.description: app.MathScripts:Add(pf.Enums.MathScriptTypeEnum.<Type>) creates a result script whose Lua code (Script property) must return a DataSet; Run() executes it and the script then behaves like a result that can be plotted, queried with GetDataSet() and frozen with StoreData(). ms:Run(); ms.DataSetAvailable; d = ms:GetDataSet(); s = ms:StoreData(); ms.Label; ms:Duplicate(); ms:Delete()

parameters.description: Lua source; fetch inputs with pf.<ResultType>.GetDataSet("model.config.request") and return the result.

parameters.name: Label
parameters.description: Default labels FarfieldMath1, CustomMath1 ...; used when referencing the script result elsewhere.

for f = 1, #d.Axes["Frequency"] do for t = 1, #d.Axes["Theta"] do for p = 1, #d.Axes["Phi"] do
  d[f][t][p].EFieldTheta = d[f][t][p].EFieldTheta * 2
end end end
return d
]]
ms:Run()
print(ms.Label, ms:GetDataSet()[1][19][1].EFieldTheta:Magnitude())  -- FarfieldMath1 1.68

tools.name: Trace formatting (Label rules, Line, Markers, Legend, Sampling, Math expression, GetProperties/SetProperties)

GetProperties() returns a Lua table of the whole state that SetProperties() re-applies, which is the quickest way to copy formatting between traces, plots and graphs.
tools.usage:
t.Label = "Gain_phi0"; t.Line.Weight = 2; t.Line.Colour; t.Markers.Symbol; t.Legend.Text = "..."
t.Sampling.Method; t.Sampling.Resolution
t.Math.Enabled = true; t.Math.Expression = "self + 3"
props = t:GetProperties(); other:SetProperties(props)

parameters.name: Label
parameters.description: Must be a valid identifier-like label (letters, digits, underscore); 'Gain phi=0' fails with Error 17002 ... is not a valid label. Use Legend.Text for free text.

parameters.name: GetProperties keys (trace)
parameters.description: Axes, DataSource, IndependentAxis, Label, Legend, Line, Markers, Math, Quantity, Sampling, Visible.

tools.example:
t.Label = "Gain_phi0"
t.Legend.Text = "Gain, phi = 0 deg"
t.Line.Weight = 2
t.Math.Enabled = true
t.Math.Expression = "self + 3"
local props = t:GetProperties()
t2 = g.Traces:Add(cfg.FarFields[2])
t2:SetProperties(props)
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: Error 17002 for a label with spaces/equals, Line.Colour (#0070C0), Line.Weight, Sampling (AutoSample, 100), Math.Expression 'self + 3', GetProperties key list, SetProperties round trip on a 3D plot. TraceMarkersFormat has no Visible property (use DensityOption/Symbol).

tools.name: Graph axes, title, legend and normalisation (HorizontalAxis, VerticalAxis, Range, DynamicRange, Legend.Position)
tools.description: Cartesian graphs expose HorizontalAxis and VerticalAxis objects (Range with AutoRangeEnabled/Min/Max, LogScaled, ReversedOrder, MajorGrid spacing, MinorGridSubdivisions, Title with Caption/AutoCaptionEnabled, Labels; VerticalAxis adds DynamicRange), Title and Footer text boxes, a Legend (Position via GraphLegendPositionEnum, NumberOfColumns, CustomPositionX/Y), Normalisation (Enabled, Method) and BackColour/GreyscaleEnabled. Fixing axis ranges makes exported images comparable between runs.
tools.usage:
g.VerticalAxis.Range.AutoRangeEnabled = false; g.VerticalAxis.Range.Min = -20; g.VerticalAxis.Range.Max = 5
g.VerticalAxis.DynamicRange; g.HorizontalAxis.LogScaled = true; g.HorizontalAxis.Title.Caption = "Frequency"
g.Title.Text = "..."; g.Legend.Position = pf.Enums.GraphLegendPositionEnum.OverlayTopRight
g.Normalisation.Enabled = true; g.WindowTitle = "GainCut"

parameters.name: DynamicRange
parameters.description: Vertical dB dynamic range for auto-ranged dB plots (default 100).

parameters.name: Normalisation.Method
parameters.description: NormalisationMethodEnum (default AllTraces).

parameters.name: WindowTitle
parameters.description: Also the graph label used for app.CartesianGraphs["..."] and for image file names in ExportAllWindowsAsImages.

tools.example:
g = app.CartesianGraphs:Add()
g.WindowTitle = "GainCut"
g.Title.Text = "Dipole gain"
g.VerticalAxis.Range.AutoRangeEnabled = false
g.VerticalAxis.Range.Min = -20
g.VerticalAxis.Range.Max = 5
g.Legend.Position = pf.Enums.GraphLegendPositionEnum.OverlayTopRight
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: Range Min/Max, DynamicRange = 100, Title.Text, Legend.Position OverlayTopRight, Normalisation (false / AllTraces), WindowTitle rename and lookup by title. The axis title text property is Caption (Title.Text on an axis returns nil).

tools.name: Graph annotations, text boxes and arrows (AddGlobalMaximum, AddHalfPowerBeamwidthAnnotation, AddBandwidthAnnotation, Shapes:AddTextBox, Arrows:AddArrow)
tools.description: graph.Annotations adds automatic markers bound to a trace: AddGlobalMaximum/AddGlobalMinimum, AddValueAtHorizontalPosition, AddIndependentValue, local maxima/minima finders, beamwidth annotations (AddHalfPowerBeamwidthAnnotation, AddFirstNullBeamwidthAnnotation, AddNullToNullBeamwidthAnnotation, AddBeamwidthAnnotation), AddSideLobeLevelAnnotation, bandwidth annotations (AddBandwidth3dBAnnotation, AddBandwidth10dBAnnotation, AddBandwidth15dBAnnotation, AddBandwidthAnnotation with a level) and AddDeltaAnnotation. annotation:GetValues() returns the computed numbers as a table, so beamwidths and bandwidths can be read from a script. graph.Shapes adds text boxes, rectangles and circles and graph.Arrows adds arrows and lines.
tools.usage:
a = g.Annotations:AddHalfPowerBeamwidthAnnotation(trace); vals = a:GetValues(); vals.dx
a = g.Annotations:AddBandwidthAnnotation(trace, pf.Enums.AnnotationBandwidthTypeEnum.PassiveReflection, -10)
a = g.Annotations:AddGlobalMaximum(trace)
g.Shapes:AddTextBox(text[, x, y]); g.Shapes:AddRectangle(x, y); g.Shapes:AddCircle(x, y)
g.Arrows:AddArrow(x1, y1, x2, y2); g.Arrows:AddDoubleHeadArrow(...); g.Arrows:AddLine(...)

parameters.name: GetValues() keys (beamwidth)
parameters.description: dx (beamwidth), p1/p2_axis_value_independent, p1/p2_axis_value_dependent, axis unit symbols and scales.

parameters.name: AnnotationBandwidthTypeEnum
parameters.description: PassiveReflection or PassiveTransmission.

parameters.name: AnnotationRelativeTypeEnum
parameters.description: RelativeToGlobalMax or RelativeToGlobalMin for the local extremum/beamwidth finders.

tools.example:
t = g.Traces:Add(cfg.FarFields[1]); t.IndependentAxis = "Theta"; t:SetFixedAxisValue("Phi", 0, "deg")
t.Quantity.Type = pf.Enums.FarFieldQuantityTypeEnum.Gain; t.Quantity.ValuesScaledToDB = true
local a = g.Annotations:AddHalfPowerBeamwidthAnnotation(t)
print(a:GetValues().dx)  -- 78.94 deg for the half-wave dipole
g.Shapes:AddTextBox("HPBW check", 0.1, 0.1)
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: AddGlobalMaximum (SimpleAnnotation, text 'Maximum: (%x, %y)'), AddHalfPowerBeamwidthAnnotation with GetValues (dx = 78.94 deg), AddBandwidthAnnotation on a reflection-coefficient trace, Shapes:AddTextBox, Arrows:AddArrow. The other Add* names are from the ResultAnnotationCollection reference.

tools.name: Graph conversion and export (DuplicateAsPolar, DuplicateAsSmith, DuplicateAsCartesian, ExportImage formats, ExportTraces, BlockGraphRedraws)
tools.description: Cartesian graphs convert with DuplicateAsPolar (only when the horizontal axis is an angle) and DuplicateAsSmith (only for impedance-type traces); polar graphs and Smith charts convert back with DuplicateAsCartesian. ExportImage(filenameWithoutExtension, format[, width, height]) writes png, jpg, bmp or pdf images, ExportTraces(filename, samples) writes all traces as a tab-separated .dat file, and BlockGraphRedraws/UnblockGraphRedraws speed up scripts that add many traces. SetSize, SetPosition, Maximise, ZoomToExtents and Close manage the window.
tools.usage:
pg = g:DuplicateAsPolar(); sc = g:DuplicateAsSmith(); cg = pg:DuplicateAsCartesian(); g:Duplicate()
g:ExportImage(filename, "png" | "jpg" | "bmp" | "pdf"[, width, height])
g:ExportTraces(filename, samples)  -- writes filename.dat
g:BlockGraphRedraws(); ... ; g:UnblockGraphRedraws(); g:SetSize(w, h); g:ZoomToExtents()

parameters.name: fileformat
parameters.description: png, jpg, bmp and pdf verified; 'svg' raises 'The file format "svg" is invalid.'

parameters.name: samples (ExportTraces)
parameters.description: Samples per trace for continuous data.

tools.example:
g:SetSize(800, 500)
g:ExportImage([[D:/work/gain_cut]], "png", 900, 600)
g:ExportTraces([[D:/work/gain_cut_traces]], 73)  -- gain_cut_traces.dat: Theta[deg] and one column per trace
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1 (software rendering in --non-interactive mode): ExportImage png/jpg/bmp/pdf, svg rejected, ExportTraces .dat content, BlockGraphRedraws/UnblockGraphRedraws. DuplicateAsPolar on a frequency-axis trace fails with Error 16338 (horizontal axis cannot be converted to a polar graph); DuplicateAsSmith on a gain trace fails with Error 16340.

tools.name: PolarGraph and SmithChart objects (Orientation, Direction, RadialAxis, AngularAxis, GridType)
tools.description: app.PolarGraphs:Add() creates polar pattern plots with Orientation (PolarGraphOrientationEnum: Auto, ZeroAtTop, ZeroAtRight, ZeroAtBottom, ZeroAtLeft), Direction (Clockwise, Anticlockwise), RadialAxis, AngularAxis, Grid and Normalisation. app.SmithCharts:Add() creates Smith charts for excitation, load and S-parameter traces with GridType (Impedance or Admittance) and resistance/reactance axis fonts; excitation traces on a Smith chart are ExcitationSmithTrace objects.
tools.usage:
pg = app.PolarGraphs:Add(); pt = pg.Traces:Add(cfg.FarFields[1]); pt.IndependentAxis = "Theta"; pg.Orientation = pf.Enums.PolarGraphOrientationEnum.ZeroAtTop
sc = app.SmithCharts:Add(); st = sc.Traces:Add(cfg.Excitations[1]); sc.GridType = pf.Enums.GridTypeEnum.Admittance

parameters.name: Orientation
parameters.description: Where 0 deg is drawn; default Auto.

parameters.name: GridType
parameters.description: GridTypeEnum.Impedance or Admittance.

tools.example:
pg = app.PolarGraphs:Add()
pt = pg.Traces:Add(cfg.FarFields[1])
pt.IndependentAxis = "Theta"
pt:SetFixedAxisValue("Phi", 90, "deg")
pg.Orientation = pf.Enums.PolarGraphOrientationEnum.ZeroAtTop
pg:ExportImage([[D:/work/polar]], "png", 600, 600)
sc = app.SmithCharts:Add()
print(sc.Traces:Add(cfg.Excitations[1]).Type)  -- ExcitationSmithTrace
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: PolarGraphs:Add with a far-field trace and exported png, Orientation read (Auto) and set, the Orientation/Direction/GridType enum members, SmithCharts:Add with ExcitationSmithTrace. Polar graphs also offer AddChartImageForTrace.

tools.name: CartesianSurfaceGraph and math traces (app.CartesianSurfaceGraphs:Add, Plots:Add, graph:AddMathTrace)
tools.description: Cartesian surface graphs draw a result as a colour map over two independent axes (e.g. theta versus phi of a far field, or frequency versus angle); the plot object (FarFieldSurfacePlot etc.) has HorizontalIndependentAxis, VerticalIndependentAxis, SwitchIndependentAxes(), fixed-axis methods and a legend. A math trace (graph:AddMathTrace()) plots a formula in x on a Cartesian or polar graph, e.g. a mask or limit line, via its Expression property.
tools.usage:
sg = app.CartesianSurfaceGraphs:Add(); sp = sg.Plots:Add(cfg.FarFields[1]); sp.HorizontalIndependentAxis; sp.VerticalIndependentAxis; sp:SwitchIndependentAxes(); sg.LockedAspectRatio
mt = g:AddMathTrace(); mt.Expression = "-10"

parameters.name: LockedAspectRatio
parameters.description: LockedAspectRatioEnum: Auto, Off, On.

parameters.name: MathTrace.Expression
parameters.description: Expression in x (the horizontal axis), e.g. 'sin(x)' or a constant limit.

tools.example:
sg = app.CartesianSurfaceGraphs:Add()
sp = sg.Plots:Add(cfg.FarFields[1])
print(sp.Type, sp.HorizontalIndependentAxis, sp.VerticalIndependentAxis)  -- FarFieldSurfacePlot Theta Phi
mt = app.CartesianGraphs[1]:AddMathTrace()
mt.Expression = "sin(x)"
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: surface graph with a FarFieldSurfacePlot (Theta/Phi defaults) and AddMathTrace returning a MathTrace with the Expression set.

tools.name: View object and 3D result plots (Views:Add, Plots:Add, PlotType, Legend.LinearRange, Visualisation, Contours, SetViewDirection)
tools.description: 3D views (app.Views) show the model mesh with result plots: Plots:Add(result) returns FarField3DPlot, NearField3DPlot, SurfaceCurrents3DPlot, ErrorEstimate3DPlot, SAR3DPlot, Ray3DPlot or CustomData3DPlot objects. Plots choose PlotType from PlotTypesAvailable (far field '3D surface', 'Phi cut', 'Theta cut'; planar near field 'XY-surface'), fix axes with SetFixedAxisValue, set a fixed legend range and tune Visualisation (Opacity, FlatShaded, Size), Contours, IsoSurface and Arrows. The view itself has SetViewDirection, Format (ThetaDirection, PhiDirection, Rotation, ZoomDistance), MeshRendering (ModelOpacity ...), ZoomToExtents, Duplicate and ExportImage.
tools.usage:
v = app.Views[1] | app.Views:Add(cfg) | app.Views:Add()
p = v.Plots:Add(result); p.PlotType = "Phi cut"; p:SetFixedAxisValue("Frequency", 7.5, "GHz")
p.Legend.LinearRange.Type = pf.Enums.LinearScaleRangeTypeEnum.Fixed; p.Legend.LinearRange.FixedRangeMin = -20; p.Legend.LinearRange.FixedRangeMax = 10
p.Visualisation.Opacity = 50; v:SetViewDirection(pf.Enums.ViewDirectionEnum.Isometric); v.Format.ThetaDirection = 60
v:ZoomToExtents(); v:ExportImage(filename, "png", w, h)

parameters.name: ViewDirectionEnum
parameters.description: Back, Bottom, Front, Isometric, Left, Right, Top.

parameters.name: NearField3DPlot:ExportIsoSurfaceToSTL(filename)
parameters.description: Writes the iso-surface as STL (from the API reference).

tools.example:
v = app.Views[1]
p = v.Plots:Add(cfg.FarFields[1])
p.Quantity.Type = pf.Enums.FarFieldQuantityTypeEnum.Gain
p.Quantity.ValuesScaledToDB = true
p.Legend.LinearRange.Type = pf.Enums.LinearScaleRangeTypeEnum.Fixed
p.Legend.LinearRange.FixedRangeMin = -20
p.Legend.LinearRange.FixedRangeMax = 10
v:SetViewDirection(pf.Enums.ViewDirectionEnum.Isometric)
v:ZoomToExtents()
v:ExportImage([[D:/work/pattern3d]], "png", 800, 600)
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: Views:Add(cfg) (title 'dipole3002'), FarField3DPlot PlotTypesAvailable, NearField3DPlot 'XY-surface', SurfaceCurrents3DPlot fixed axis Frequency, fixed legend range, Visualisation.Opacity, Contours (Visible false, Type SpecifyByCount), Format.ThetaDirection, MeshRendering.ModelOpacity, ViewDirectionEnum members, ExportImage png in non-interactive mode. The first view of a model is created automatically on OpenFile and titled '<model>1'.

tools.name: View animation export (View.Animation, ExportAnimation with GIF/AVI/MKV/MOV)
tools.description: view.Animation (View3DAnimationFormat) sets the animation type (AnimationTypeEnum, e.g. PhiRotate, Phase) and step settings (PhaseStepSize, PhiStepSize, ThetaStepSize, FrequencyRate, ContinuousFrequencySamples, RealTimeDuration). view:ExportAnimation(filename, format, quality, width, height, framerate) renders the animation to a GIF, AVI, MKV or MOV file without user interaction, e.g. rotating far-field patterns or current phase animations for reports.
tools.usage:
v.Animation.Type = pf.Enums.AnimationTypeEnum.PhiRotate | Phase ...
v:ExportAnimation(filename, pf.Enums.AnimationFormatEnum.GIF | AVI | MKV | MOV, pf.Enums.AnimationQualityEnum.Low | Normal | High, width, height, framerate)

parameters.name: AnimationFormatEnum
parameters.description: AVI, GIF, MKV, MOV (2026.1 members).

parameters.name: AnimationQualityEnum
parameters.description: Low, Normal, High.

parameters.name: framerate
parameters.description: Frames per second of the written file.

tools.example:
v = app.Views[1]
v.Plots:Add(cfg.FarFields[1])
v.Animation.Type = pf.Enums.AnimationTypeEnum.PhiRotate
v:ExportAnimation([[D:/work/anim]], pf.Enums.AnimationFormatEnum.GIF, pf.Enums.AnimationQualityEnum.Normal, 320, 240, 10)  -- anim.gif
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1 in --non-interactive mode (anim.gif written); default Animation.Type of a new view is PhiRotate. Video formats use the ffmpeg.exe shipped in the Feko bin folder.

tools.name: Windows collection and batch image export (app.Windows, GetActiveWindow, ExportAllWindowsAsImages)
tools.description: app.Windows lists every graph and 3D view as Window objects (Type CartesianGraph, PolarGraph, SmithChart, View ...), with GetActiveWindow() for the current one. app:ExportAllWindowsAsImages(directory, format[, width, height]) writes one image per window named after its WindowTitle, which is the simplest way to dump every plot of a session after a batch solve. The target directory must already exist.
tools.usage:
app.Windows.Count; app.Windows[i].Type; app.Windows:GetActiveWindow()
app:ExportAllWindowsAsImages(directory, "png" | "jpg" ...[, width, height])

parameters.name: directory
parameters.description: Existing folder (with or without trailing slash); a missing folder raises 'The directory ... doesn't exist.'

parameters.name: fileformat
parameters.description: Image extension such as png or jpg.

tools.example:
lfs = require("lfs")
lfs.mkdir([[D:/work/images]])
app:ExportAllWindowsAsImages([[D:/work/images]], "png", 1200, 800)
-- writes GainCut.png, Polar graph1.png, dipole3001.png ...
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: Windows.Count/Type list, GetActiveWindow, ExportAllWindowsAsImages png and jpg (with size) into an existing folder, and the error for a non-existent folder.

tools.name: ExportData samples rule and export file names (.ffe, .efe/.hfe, .os/.ol, .sNp, .dat, .mat)
tools.description: All POSTFEKO ExportData/Export* calls take the file name without extension and append it themselves: far fields .ffe, near fields .efe/.hfe, currents .os (surface) and .ol (wire), Touchstone .s<N>p, graph traces .dat. The trailing samples argument must be at least 2 even for single-frequency discrete results (it only controls re-sampling of continuous data). DataSet:ExportMatFile and pf.MatIO use the file name exactly as given (include .mat).
tools.usage:
ff:ExportData("name", FarFieldsExportTypeEnum, 2) -> name.ffe
nf:ExportData("name", NearFieldsExportTypeEnum, 2) -> name.efe / name.hfe
sc:ExportData("name", CurrentsExportTypeEnum, 2) -> name.os + name.ol
sp:ExportData("name", FrequencyUnitEnum, NetworkParameterTypeEnum, NetworkParameterFormatEnum[, Zref], 2) -> name.sNp
g:ExportTraces("name", n) -> name.dat

parameters.name: samples = 1
parameters.description: Rejected: '1 is an invalid sample count. The least number of samples allowed is 2.'

parameters.name: string-only call
parameters.description: ExportData(path) without the enum and sample arguments is rejected.

tools.example:
ff:ExportData([[D:/work/dipole_ff]], pf.Enums.FarFieldsExportTypeEnum.Gain, 2)
cfg.Excitations[1]:ExportData([[D:/work/dipole_s]], pf.Enums.FrequencyUnitEnum.MHz, pf.Enums.NetworkParameterTypeEnum.Scattering, pf.Enums.NetworkParameterFormatEnum.RI, 50, 2)
-- -> dipole_ff.ffe, dipole_s.s1p
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1 for every extension listed. Some older examples (including the overview entry in this catalog) pass 1 as the sample count; that fails on 2026.1.

tools.name: pf.MatIO namespace (ExportMatFile, GetNames, ReadMatFile, ReadMatFileStructure, ReadMatFileToTable)
tools.description: pf.MatIO reads and writes MATLAB .mat files from POSTFEKO scripts: ExportMatFile accepts a Matrix, ComplexMatrix, Lua table or DataSet; GetNames lists the variables in a file that can be read back into a DataSet; ReadMatFile(file) returns the whole file as a Lua table while ReadMatFile(file, name) returns one DataSet; ReadMatFileStructure and ReadMatFileToTable give the layout or a single variable as a table. It is the standard bridge to MATLAB post-processing.
tools.usage:
pf.MatIO.ExportMatFile(datasetOrMatrixOrTable, filename, varname)
names = pf.MatIO.GetNames(filename)
tbl = pf.MatIO.ReadMatFile(filename); ds = pf.MatIO.ReadMatFile(filename, name)
pf.MatIO.ReadMatFileStructure(filename); pf.MatIO.ReadMatFileToTable(filename, name)

parameters.name: name (ReadMatFile)
parameters.description: Must be one of the strings returned by GetNames, e.g. 'ff.Data.GainFactor'; the bare variable name is rejected.

parameters.name: DataSet layout in .mat
parameters.description: A data set 'ff' is stored as ff.Axes[k].Values and ff.Data.<Quantity> fields.

tools.example:
ds = cfg.FarFields[1]:GetDataSet()
ds:ExportMatFile([[D:/work/ff.mat]], "ff")
for _, n in ipairs(pf.MatIO.GetNames([[D:/work/ff.mat]])) do print(n) end
-- ff.Axes[2].Values ... ff.Data.EFieldTheta ... ff.Data.GainFactor
local t = pf.MatIO.ReadMatFile([[D:/work/ff.mat]])  -- table with key 'ff'
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: ExportMatFile, GetNames output, ReadMatFile(file) and ReadMatFileStructure(file) returning tables keyed 'ff', and 'ff is not a valid dataset name. Only names obtained via pf.MatIO.GetNames may be used.' for ReadMatFile(file, 'ff').

tools.name: pf.Archive and pf.DRE namespaces (Zip, UnZip, InspectZip; DRE ImportDataSet/ExportDataSet)
tools.description: pf.Archive creates and extracts zip archives from scripts (Zip(zipfile, list) adds files or folders, UnZip(zipfile, destination[, files]) extracts, InspectZip lists contents), handy for bundling exports of a batch run. pf.DRE reads and writes the DRE (Daimler Result Exchange) format: DiscoverHierarchy lists a file's contents, ImportDataSet/StoreData read a data set (optionally with pf.DRE.ImportSettings), and ExportDataSet writes a Feko DataSet under a given path.
tools.usage:
pf.Archive.Zip(zipfile, {file1, folder2}); pf.Archive.UnZip(zipfile, destination); pf.Archive.InspectZip(zipfile)
pf.DRE.DiscoverHierarchy(filename[, startPoint]); ds = pf.DRE.ImportDataSet(filename, dataSetPath[, settings]); pf.DRE.ExportDataSet(ds, filename, dataSetPath); pf.DRE.StoreData(filename, dataSetPath, type)

parameters.name: Zip behaviour
parameters.description: If the zip exists, files are added; entries with the same name are replaced.

parameters.name: dataSetPath (DRE)
parameters.description: Hierarchical label inside the DRE file.

tools.example:
pf.Archive.Zip([[D:/work/results.zip]], {[[D:/work/dipole_ff.ffe]], [[D:/work/dipole_s.s1p]]})
for _, f in ipairs(pf.Archive.InspectZip([[D:/work/results.zip]])) do print(f) end
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: pf.Archive.Zip and InspectZip (InspectZip returns the stored path of each file); pf.DRE functions exist but were not exercised (no DRE file available) - signatures are from the API reference.

tools.name: QuickReport and ReportTemplate objects (CreateQuickReport, SetPageIncluded, SetPageTitle, Reports:Add, TagSettings, Generate)
tools.description: app:CreateQuickReport(filename, pf.Enums.ReportDocumentTypeEnum.PDF | MSWord | MSPowerPoint) returns a QuickReport with one page per window: DocumentHeading, PageOrientation (Landscape/Portrait), ImageFormat, ImageSize, ReportPageOptions and SetPageIncluded/SetPageTitle/SetPageCaption per window title, then Generate() or GenerateAndOpen(). app.Reports:Add(templateFile, type) creates a ReportTemplate from a Word/PowerPoint template whose tags are mapped to windows via TagSettings; Generate(filename) fills it, and ImportReportTemplate/ExportReportTemplate move template definitions between sessions.
tools.usage:
r = app:CreateQuickReport(filename, pf.Enums.ReportDocumentTypeEnum.PDF); r.DocumentHeading = "..."; r.PageOrientation = pf.Enums.ReportOrientationEnum.Landscape; r:SetPageIncluded(windowTitle, false); r:Generate()
tpl = app.Reports:Add(templateFile, pf.Enums.ReportDocumentTypeEnum.MSWord); tpl.Tags; tpl.TagSettings[1].Window = "GainCut"; tpl:Generate(outFile)

parameters.name: ReportPageOptions
parameters.description: List of window titles that become pages.

parameters.name: MSWord / MSPowerPoint
parameters.description: Require Office (check app.MSWordInstalled / app.MSPowerPointInstalled); PDF does not.

tools.example:
r = app:CreateQuickReport([[D:/work/quick_report]], pf.Enums.ReportDocumentTypeEnum.PDF)
r.DocumentHeading = "Dipole results"
r:SetPageIncluded("Cartesian graph2", false)
r:Generate()  -- quick_report.pdf
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: a PDF quick report generated headless with four window pages; ReportOrientationEnum members Landscape/Portrait. ReportTemplate methods are from the API reference (a sample template StartupModel.dotx ships in FEKO_HOME/shared/Resources/Automation).

tools.name: pf.Launcher.Run (run external programs and Feko components from a POSTFEKO script)
tools.description: pf.Launcher.Run(command) or pf.Launcher.Run(executable, argumentList) starts a process, waits for it and returns a LaunchResult with Succeeded, ExitCode, Output, Errors, Warnings and Notices. Together with model.Launcher (RunFEKO, RunPREFEKO, GetCommandRunFEKO) it lets a POSTFEKO script re-solve a model, call runfeko on another file or run converters before post-processing.
tools.usage:
r = pf.Launcher.Run(commandString) | pf.Launcher.Run(executable, {arg1, arg2})
r.Succeeded; r.ExitCode; r.Output; r.Errors; r.Warnings; r.Notices
r = app.Models[1].Launcher:RunFEKO()

parameters.name: executable
parameters.description: Full path; Lua long-bracket strings avoid escaping backslashes.

parameters.name: arguments
parameters.description: Lua list of argument strings.

tools.example:
local r = pf.Launcher.Run([[C:/Program Files/Altair/2026.1/feko/bin/prefeko.exe]], {"--version"})
print(r.ExitCode, string.sub(r.Output, 1, 60))
-- 100  Altair Feko - PREFEKO Version 2026.1-8642 ...
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1: pf.Launcher.Run with an argument list captured prefeko's version banner; prefeko --version returns exit code 100, so Succeeded was false - check Output rather than Succeeded for such utilities. Re-solving from POSTFEKO overwrites the .bof that is loaded; call app:ReloadChangedFiles() afterwards.

tools.name: Script environment: global keywords and bundled Lua modules (FEKO_HOME, FEKO_USER_HOME, SESSION_PATH, printlist, inspect, lfs, luaxml, pl, winapi, luacom)
tools.description: CADFEKO and POSTFEKO scripts run Lua 5.1 with the standard math, string, table, os, io and debug libraries plus Feko globals: i and j (sqrt(-1)), FEKO_HOME, FEKO_USER_HOME, SESSION_PATH and SESSION_NAME (math scripts), printlist (prints key/value lists) and inspect (prints nested tables). Extra modules ship with Feko and are loaded with require: lfs (LuaFileSystem), luaxml, pl (Penlight), winapi and luacom (COM automation of Excel/Word on Windows). Further module search paths are set under Settings > Preferences > Default settings > Scripting.
tools.usage:
local lfs = require("lfs"); lfs.mkdir(path); lfs.currentdir()
require("luaxml"); local path = require("pl.path"); local w = require("winapi"); require("luacom")
print(FEKO_HOME, FEKO_USER_HOME); printlist(list); inspect(tbl)

parameters.name: FEKO_USER_HOME
parameters.description: Per-user settings folder, e.g. C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Roaming/feko/2026.1_<hash>.

parameters.name: luacom
parameters.description: COM client; luacom.CreateObject("Excel.Application") drives Excel.

tools.example:
local lfs = require("lfs")
print(lfs.currentdir())  -- the script's folder
local path = require("pl.path")
print(path.basename([[D:/a/b/c.txt]]))  -- c.txt
print(FEKO_HOME)  -- C:\Program Files\Altair\2026.1\feko
inspect({a = 1, b = {2, 3}})
tools.notes: Run-verified on 2026.1 in POSTFEKO --non-interactive: _VERSION 'Lua 5.1', require of lfs, luaxml, pl.path, winapi and luacom, FEKO_HOME, FEKO_USER_HOME, i printing '0 + 1i', printlist and inspect output. SESSION_PATH/SESSION_NAME are documented for math scripts and were not probed.
